title: Mock recitation against the rubric: record and plan
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 1: Tajweed mastery and Al-Kahf consolidation
source: Written for quran/y11 lesson 14 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Mock week recitation against the rubric rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 14. The recitation is spoken, live and from memory. Your examiner (a partner or the teacher) scores each row of the rubric from 1 to 4. Answer the rule questions in writing while you wait for your turn.

bullets: Steady pace; stop only at the ends of ayat
If you lose your place, pause and restart the ayah calmly

questions.q: What is a saktah, and where is the saktah in Al-Kahf 18:1 to 10?
questions.a: A brief pause without taking a new breath; in 18:1: عِوَجَا ۜ قَيِّمًا.

questions.q: Name the rule in «صَعِيدًۭا جُرُزًا» (18:8) and say how it is read.
questions.a: Ikhfa: the tanween is hidden with a light two-count hum before the jeem.
Rashadaa: the fathatan becomes a long alif sound (madd 'iwad).

questions.q: What does the small stop sign م (lazim) mean?
Why must lahn jali (a clear mistake) be fixed before lahn khafi?
questions.a: Lahn jali changes a letter, vowel or word and can change the meaning, so it is fixed first; lahn khafi is a slip in a tajweed rule.

box.title: My plan to the final assessment (weakest portion daily, one rule family a week)

markScheme.a: Score each rubric row 1 to 4 (4 secure, 3 mostly secure, 2 developing, 1 not yet). Total out of 20. Record scores and one target in the portal.
